system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- For GROUNDED, use "hold" when unreadable PDF symbols prevent verification; explain what is needed. Use fail only when the available evidence is sufficient to determine that the claim is unsupported. This hold rule takes precedence over the strictness rule. Judge other checks independently using their listed values; do not invent missing facts.
- Be strict within each check's allowed values. Do not turn an inability to verify GROUNDED into revise or fail; use hold as defined above.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail / hold]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom, including its specificity, causal force, assumptions, and certainty. pass = fully stated. revise = partly stated (the atom adds, drops, or strengthens something; say what). fail = not stated when the available evidence permits a judgment. hold = unreadable symbols prevent verification. For pass or revise, put the supporting evidence ids in cite.
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately. Evidence spanning more than three sentences is not by itself a reason to split or revise an atom.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge. fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = an isolated study finding, conjecture, or author-specific opinion, classification, or recommendation, even if attribution was removed. Explicitly scoped established facts about a formalism or architecture and conditional theoretical results remain eligible.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a topic whose assessable content is restricted to excluded study-specific findings or author-specific positions. A named formalism, system, or architecture is not disqualified solely for being specific if its scoped conceptual facts are source-independent.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}
user:
CONCEPT: Minimal fibration
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: Cover minimal J-fibrations in the simplicial and dendroidal settings through fibrewise homotopy relative to boundaries, equality of equivalent simplices versus equality up to tree automorphisms, rigidity and minimal deformation retracts under their stated hypotheses. Include minimal Kan fibrations and the differing base-change conditions, retaining normality and stabilizer assumptions in the dendroidal results; exclude unrelated absolute minimal-category proofs and later chapters.

ATOMS:
- MATH-TOP-C10-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: For a J-fibration $p:X\to S$ and a monomorphism $A\to B$, two maps $f,g:B\to X$ with $pf=pg$ are fibrewise J-homotopic relative to $A$ if there is a homotopy $h:J\times B\to X$ from $f$ to $g$ that restricts to the constant homotopy on $A$ and whose composite with $p$ is the constant homotopy $J\times B\to B\to S$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0223-s17] For a J-ﬁbration p : X →S and a monomorphism i : A →B, we call two maps f, g : B →X over S (i.e., p f = pg) ﬁbrewise J-homotopic relative to A if there is a homotopy h : J × B →X from f to g which restricts to the constant homotopy J × A →A →X on A and composes to the constant homotopy J × B →B →S to S.
- MATH-TOP-C10-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: For a J-fibration $p:X\to S$ between ∞-operads, $p$ is a minimal J-fibration if for any two dendrices $x,y\in X_T$ that are fibrewise J-homotopic relative to $\partial\Omega[T]$ (fibrewise J-equivalent), there exists an automorphism $\alpha$ of the tree $T$ with $\alpha^*x=y$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0273-s11] (a) Two dendrices x, y ∈XT are ﬁbrewise J-equivalent if, when viewed as maps Ω[T] →X, they are ﬁbrewise J-homotopic relative to the boundary ∂Ω[T].
    [MATH-TOP-p0273-s12] (In particular, px = py and x and y agree on ∂Ω[T].) (b) The map p : X →S is a minimal J-ﬁbration if for any two ﬁbrewise J-equivalent dendrices x, y ∈XT, there exists an automorphism α of T so that α∗x = y.
- MATH-TOP-C10-S1-03 | S1
  ATOM: For a J-fibration $p:X\to S$ between ∞-categories (or a Kan fibration between general simplicial sets), $p$ is a minimal J-fibration (respectively a minimal Kan fibration) if any two fibrewise J-equivalent $n$-simplices of $X$, meaning fibrewise J-homotopic relative to $\partial\Delta[n]$ when viewed as maps $\Delta[n]\to X$, are equal.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0224-s06] Deﬁnition 5.69 Let p : X →S be a J-ﬁbration between ∞-categories or a Kan ﬁbration between general simplicial sets.
    [MATH-TOP-p0224-s07] (a) Two n-simplices x, y ∈Xn are ﬁbrewise J-equivalent if, when viewed as maps ∆[n] →X, these simplices are ﬁbrewise J-homotopic relative to ∂∆[n].
    [MATH-TOP-p0224-s08] (In particular, px = py and x and y agree on ∂∆[n].) (b) The map p : X →S is a minimal J-ﬁbration (or a minimal Kan ﬁbration if p is a Kan ﬁbration) if any two ﬁbrewise J-equivalent simplices are equal.
- MATH-TOP-C10-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: For a J-fibration $p:X\to S$ between ∞-categories there exists a minimal J-fibration $q:M\to S$ that is a fibrewise J-deformation retract of $X\to S$, and the retraction is a trivial fibration; the same holds for a Kan fibration between arbitrary simplicial sets.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0224-s18] Theorem 5.71 Let p : X →S be a J-ﬁbration between ∞-categories.
    [MATH-TOP-p0224-s19] Then there exists a minimal J-ﬁbration q : M →S which is a ﬁbrewise J-deformation retract of X →S.
    [MATH-TOP-p0224-s20] Moreover, the retraction is a trivial ﬁbration.
    [MATH-TOP-p0224-s21] The same applies to a Kan ﬁbration between arbitrary simplicial sets.
- MATH-TOP-C10-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: Any fibrewise J-homotopy equivalence $\varphi:X\to Y$ over $S$ between two minimal J-fibrations $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ of $\infty$-categories is an isomorphism, and the same holds for minimal Kan fibrations between general simplicial sets.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0224-s14] Proposition 5.70 Let p : X →S and q : Y →S be minimal J-ﬁbrations between ∞-categories.
    [MATH-TOP-p0224-s15] Then any ﬁbrewise J-homotopy equivalence ϕ : X →Y over S is an isomorphism.
    [MATH-TOP-p0224-s16] The same is true for minimal Kan ﬁbrations between general simplicial sets.
- MATH-TOP-C10-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: If $p:X\to S$ is a minimal J-fibration between $\infty$-categories and $f,g:T\to S$ are J-homotopic maps from an $\infty$-category $T$, then the pullbacks $f^*p$ and $g^*p$ are isomorphic minimal J-fibrations over $T$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0225-s13] Proposition 5.73 Let p : X →S be a minimal J-ﬁbration between ∞-categories.
    [MATH-TOP-p0225-s14] If f, g : T →S are two J-homotopic maps from an ∞-category T, then the pullbacks f ∗p and g∗p are isomorphic minimal J-ﬁbrations over T.
- MATH-TOP-C10-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: For simplicial sets, minimal J-fibrations are readily closed under pullback, but for dendroidal sets pullback along a map $f:S'\to S$ of $\infty$-operads preserves minimality of a minimal J-fibration $p:X\to S$ with $X$ normal only when the induced maps of stabilizers $\mathrm{Aut}(T)_x\to\mathrm{Aut}(T)_{f(x)}$ are isomorphisms, a condition automatically satisfied when $S'$ and $S$ are normal.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0277-s29] In the case of simplicial sets it was rather evident that the class of minimal J- ﬁbrations is closed under pullbacks.
    [MATH-TOP-p0277-s30] This is not quite the case for dendroidal sets.
    [MATH-TOP-p0278-s02] Lemma 6.57 Let f : S′ →S be a map of ∞-operads such that for any dendrex x ∈XT, the induced map of stabilizers Aut(T)x →Aut(T)f (x) is an isomorphism.
    [MATH-TOP-p0278-s03] If p : X →S is a minimal J-ﬁbration between ∞-operads, with X normal, then the pullback q : f ∗X →S′ is again a minimal J-ﬁbration between ∞-operads.
    [MATH-TOP-p0278-s04] In particular, note that the condition on stabilizers is automatically satisﬁed when S′ and S are normal.
- MATH-TOP-C10-S3-02 | S3
  ATOM: The dendroidal rigidity result (any fibrewise J-homotopy equivalence over $S$ between minimal J-fibrations $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ of ∞-operads is an isomorphism) requires both $X$ and $Y$ to be normal.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0273-s18] Proposition 6.54 Let p : X →S and q : Y →S be minimal J-ﬁbrations between ∞-operads and suppose both X and Y are normal.
    [MATH-TOP-p0273-s19] Then any ﬁbrewise J-homotopy equivalence X →Y over S is an isomorphism.
